newsitem.title: JORDAN: Egypt's FM says Afghan faction fighting "pathetic".
newsitem.headline: Egypt's FM says Afghan faction fighting "pathetic".

text.p: Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said on Tuesday rival Afghan factions were destroying their war-torn country with "pathetic" squabbles.
"The situation in Afghanistan is hopeless," Moussa told a U.N. workshop when asked about fighting between the purist Islamist Taleban militia and its northern opponents.
"The way the Afghan people are harming each other, forgetting about the future of their country, the rights of the people, the prosperity of their brethren, is indeed pathetic," Moussa said.
"Afghanistan is going down the drain if the war continues the way it is and it is not worth it to support one faction against the other," he added.
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates officially recognised the Taleban government last month after it forced into exile General Abdul Rashid Dostum, pillar of an anti-Taleban alliance.
But Taleban gains in the northern areas controlled by Dostum were quickly reversed and another opposition commander, Ahmad Shah Masood rejoined the fighting.
"They have to get together, those Afghani factions, and understand that their ship is sinking and if it sinks all of them are going to sink with it," said Moussa.

Egypt says many of the Islamist militants who have waged a five-year campaign of violence against its government were originally trained in Afghanistan during the mujahedeen resistance to Soviet occupation forces in the 1980s.
